quick: 30 mg PO three times daily (or 75 mg SR once daily)
Take after food to reduce GI upset
Avoid in first trimester; use only if needed
Not recommended; excreted in animal milk
Caution; dosing interval may be extended
summary: Ambroxol is a mucolytic that reduces sputum viscosity and promotes expectoration in productive cough and respiratory disorders with thick mucus. The usual adult oral dose is 30 mg three times daily (or a 75 mg sustained-release capsule once daily). It is an active metabolite of bromhexine and stimulates surfactant production. It is not FDA-approved; this record is based on EMA/SmPC and standard references.
indications: Secretolytic therapy in acute and chronic bronchopulmonary disorders associated with abnormal mucus secretion and impaired mucus transport
Productive (chesty) cough where loosening of thick mucus is required
Adjunct in chronic obstructive airway disease / chronic bronchitis exacerbations

dosage.t: Three times daily (may reduce to twice daily)
dosage.n: May start 30 mg three times daily for first days then reduce

admin: Take orally after meals to minimize gastrointestinal discomfort
Swallow sustained-release capsules whole with liquid; do not chew or crush
Maintain adequate fluid intake to support the mucolytic effect
Avoid taking at bedtime where the expectorant effect may disturb sleep
Discontinue and seek care if skin or mucosal reactions develop
moa: Ambroxol is a mucolytic that increases serous secretion, reduces the viscosity of mucus and stimulates ciliary activity, improving mucus clearance (mucociliary transport). It promotes synthesis and release of pulmonary surfactant by type II pneumocytes. Ambroxol also has local anesthetic and weak anti-inflammatory/antioxidant properties and is the active metabolite of bromhexine.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to ambroxol or excipients
relative: History of severe cutaneous reactions to ambroxol/bromhexine
Gastric or duodenal ulcer (mucolytics may disrupt the mucosal barrier)
monitor: Impaired bronchomotor/mucus clearance (risk of secretion accumulation)

preg: Avoid during the first trimester. Although clinical data have not shown clear harmful effects, use during pregnancy only if clearly necessary and after assessing benefit versus risk.
lact: Ambroxol passes into animal milk; excretion in human milk is not well characterized. Use during breastfeeding is generally not recommended.
renal: Use with caution in severe renal impairment; metabolites may accumulate. Consider dose reduction or extended dosing interval.
hepatic: Ambroxol is metabolized in the liver; use with caution in severe hepatic impairment and consider longer dosing intervals.

moderate: Antitussives (e.g., codeine, dextromethorphan) - suppressing cough while loosening mucus can cause secretion build-up; avoid concurrent use
minor: Antibiotics (amoxicillin, cefuroxime, erythromycin) - ambroxol may increase antibiotic penetration into bronchial secretions (generally beneficial)
interactions.food: Take after food to reduce gastrointestinal upset.
interactions.alcohol: No specific clinically significant interaction; moderate intake.

serious: Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis)
emergency: Severe blistering/peeling skin reaction (SJS/TEN) - stop and seek emergency care

monitoring: Skin and mucous membranes for early signs of severe cutaneous reactions
Tolerability in patients with peptic ulcer history
counsel: Take after food and drink plenty of fluids to help loosen mucus
Stop the medicine and seek urgent care if a skin rash, blistering or peeling develops
Report persistent cough beyond a few days or any worsening symptoms
pk: 6-12 hours; SR formulation allows once-daily dosing
Store at room temperature, protected from moisture and light
pearls: Not FDA-approved; this record is based on EMA-region SmPC and standard references (BNF) rather than an FDA label
Active metabolite of bromhexine with surfactant-stimulating action
Regulatory reviews flagged rare but serious cutaneous (SJS/TEN) and anaphylactic reactions - counsel patients
Avoid pairing with antitussives, which can trap loosened secretions
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is nearly time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the usual schedule; do not double up.
overdose: No specific severe overdose syndrome is described; reported effects are transient restlessness and diarrhea. Manage symptomatically and supportively. Emesis or gastric measures are not usually needed unless a very large amount was taken.
